reason: A is Material 3 on iOS: kebab/download icons, M3 filter chips, small title, tinted hero card, colored icon circles and pill badges compete. At AX-XL its balance splits mid-number ('$12,847.' / '33'). B uses an iOS large title, inset grouped list, one dominant spend figure with de-emphasized $ and cents, and calm monochrome icons. Its AX-XL layout wraps cleanly.

A has one clear focal number with a de-emphasized currency sign and cents, monochrome restraint, red used only for overspend, a native large title, and a clean reflow at AX-XL. In B the action chips wrap awkwardly and a floating Add expense button covers the budget rows. Its hero card turns light mint in dark mode, and at AX-XL the greeting truncates and the button covers the income figures.

B leads with one dominant number with smaller cents, a calm inset grouped list, a native large title, and a real over-budget row. A is busy: a heavy hero card, a wrapping chip row with Reports left alone on its own line, and a floating button over budget rows. At AX-XL that button covers income and the greeting is cut off. A's dark mode flips the hero to mint, which glares. B reflows cleanly.

A looks native: large title, inset grouped lists, system toggles and a footer note. Its realistic copy holds up, and it reflows well at AX-XL. B uses a small inline title, bordered cards, an icon in every row, a five-swatch picker and odd body letter-spacing. At AX-XL it breaks 'notification/s' mid-word, and its title doesn't scale.

B reads as native iOS: a large title, inset grouped lists, system toggles, value rows with chevrons and a footer note, all with restrained color. A uses a small inline title, bordered cards, a hand-built segmented control and accent swatches. At AX-XL, A breaks 'notification/s' mid-word, its title doesn't scale and the email is cut off. B's title scales cleanly; only its email wraps mid-word.

A shows the monthly/yearly selector with Yearly preselected, savings, and the per-month equivalent. Its type is restrained and editorial, with one accent. B has no visible plan choice, which misses the brief, and leans on a generic icon hero and tinted icon tiles. At AX-XL, B's sticky footer takes up more than half the screen. A's 'How your trial works' row gets cut off under the footer.

A shows no monthly vs yearly picker, so it misses the brief: there is only a yearly trial CTA. Its icon-tile feature list is generic, and at AX-XL the headline is clipped and the features disappear. B has a clear two-plan selector with per-month math and savings, an editorial type ramp and a well-adjusted dark mode. At AX-XL it degrades but stays scrollable.

A's realistic product-preview card is compelling, but it competes with the headline. A also clips the 'Talk, don't type' row under the CTA bar at default size. At AX-XL, A's card takes over the screen: the title truncates, the headline disappears and the mic icon sits misaligned. B is restrained, has one accent and a clean type ramp, and degrades more gracefully, though its plain feature list is generic.

A is disciplined: one orange accent, a dominant headline and a clean feature ramp. Its dark mode is a straight inversion, and at AX-XL a row clips under the footer and the secondary link disappears. B's product-preview card has more realistic content and better dark surfaces, but it pulls focus from the headline, uses purple heavily and gets cramped at AX-XL (tiny icon, truncation).

A is restrained: neutral palette, a single black CTA that inverts properly in dark mode, and native-feeling chrome. At AX-XL it wraps the title and only clips the price under the sticky bar. B layers a tinted card, a discount badge, a Save pill and an Android-style back arrow. At AX-XL it badly truncates the name, price, CTA and cart badge. B's richer commerce content doesn't make up for this.

At AX-XL, A's sticky bar fails: "Add to..." and "$139." are cut off and "No size ..." is clipped. A also has too many accents: discount badge, Save pill, rust eyebrow, cart badge, rust CTA. B is restrained, with one black CTA that carries the price and native Size/Colour rows. At AX-XL its CTA stays readable, but its own price line is clipped behind the CTA.

A feels like iOS: a bold large title, one dominant spend figure with a de-emphasized cents/currency, inset grouped lists, and a clean reflow at AX-XL. B is Material on iPhone: a small non-bold title, a download/kebab app bar and check-mark chips. At AX-XL B's balance breaks to '$12,847.' / '33' and its chips get clipped. B has richer content: daily totals and pending badges.

A is restrained and native: a large title, one dominant 21.6 km figure with a de-emphasized unit, a single accent on today's bar, and a realistic runs list. B is card soup: tinted tiles, an icon on every stat, a wash of pink and a hand-rolled header. B handles AX-XL better (A's week label and delta line wrap awkwardly), but A reads as designed.

B is restrained and native: a large title, one dominant number, a single orange accent, a quiet chart, a compact stat row and a list of real runs. A leans on tinted card soup with an icon on every tile and a small custom header. A holds up better at AX-XL, where B's week switcher and delta line wrap awkwardly. A's dark mode is warmer and more deliberately designed.

B has one primary action: the Apple button sits in a thumb-zone footer with equal Google and email options, and the full email form is left for a later step. A puts two strong primaries on one screen (black Apple and green Sign in), which makes it denser. B's copy is more specific. At AX-XL, A's icons no longer line up with the button text, and B's footer shows only Apple, with Google and email out of view.

A is very restrained and has strong hero copy, but the middle of the screen is a large empty gap, and email is only a third button. B shows a complete, native-feeling email form with grouped fields and a tuned dark-mode accent. However, its green Sign in button competes with the black Apple button. In both, the provider icons stay small at AX-XL.
